question: Should OpenClaw add `agents.list[].subagents.workspace` for same-agent default child workspace isolation, or keep explicit `agentId` profiles plus `requireAgentId` as the supported boundary?
rationale: This changes which workspace files default child subagents can read and adds public config surface, so automation should not choose the security and product policy.

options.title: Keep Explicit Profiles
options.body: Document and preserve the current model where safe isolation uses `requireAgentId` plus configured child agent profiles with their own workspaces.

options.title: Add Opt-In Workspace Override
options.body: Implement `subagents.workspace` as a strict per-agent default-child override with no effect on explicit target-agent spawns and with focused security tests.

options.title: Defer To Broader Spawn Design
options.body: Hold this until workspace, cwd, sandbox, and skill workdir isolation are designed together with https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/87253.

recommendation.title: Keep Explicit Profiles
recommendation.body: Document and preserve the current model where safe isolation uses `requireAgentId` plus configured child agent profiles with their own workspaces.

likelyOwner.reason: Current checked lines and recent subagent/config area history make this the best available routing candidate for the boundary decision.
